location.ref: Dādū Janma Līlā, the old man's blessing

paraphrase: When Dādū was eleven an old man appeared to him, took pān from his hand and put it in Dādū's mouth, touched his head, and vanished; seven years later he appeared again and completed the teaching.
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D

location.ref: Dādū Janma Līlā, the meeting with Akbar (1585)

paraphrase: Summoned to Fatehpur Sikri, Dādū spoke with the emperor Akbar over days about the one God beyond Hindu and Muslim; Akbar honoured him.
translation_basis: paraphrase from memory of the vernacular text (Phase B skeleton); to be checked against an edition in Phase D
notes: Skeleton from memory (Phase B). Narrative; gist from Callewaert's study of the Janma Līlā.
